samples.reason: This is a highly-specified generative task with strict formatting constraints (exact template, word limits, numbering, required keywords). Avocet's top-rated tasks are well-specified reformatting requests with clear completion criteria, and its Creative Generation is its strongest eval category — a good fit despite the creative angle. Both models are near-tied on capability, but the rigid format favors Avocet.

This is a creative generation task but with strict, well-specified formatting constraints (exact template, numbering, word limits, required words). Both models tie on Creative Generation within variance, and Avocet's strongest eval is Creative Generation plus it has the higher IFEval-equivalent strength on tightly-specified, clear-completion-criteria tasks. The warmth/generativity profile of Petrel offers no decisive edge here given the rigid template, so Avocet is the better fit.

This is a high-volume generative task with a strict, well-specified template (numbering, prefix, word count, emoji, keyword constraints). Avocet's top capability is Creative Generation, and the rigid completion criteria match its strength in format-adherent reformatting. IFEval is effectively a tie, so Avocet's creative edge decides it. (Avocet's self-reported aversion to open-ended work is explicitly dissociated from quality and doesn't affect output, and the tight constraints make this far from fully open-ended anyway.)
